what_this_is: Smart Radiology: four programmes in the radiology department. One ambition: get more out of every scan already taken, so patients are treated better and faster.

pillars.name: Detect earlier
pillars.what: RbFracture reads every emergency extremity film the moment it arrives and returns a flag in minutes, 24 hours a day - at 3am as at 3pm. The emergency physician gets an answer now, not a waiting report. The radiologist still decides; the flag orders the work.

pillars.name: See better
pillars.what: Routine CT becomes 3D and 4D models for planning from the scan already taken - no extra radiation, no extra appointment. Digital-first: most never need to become a printed object. Dual-energy CT shows bone-marrow oedema (the bruise inside the bone) that plain CT cannot.

pillars.name: Prepare better
pillars.what: Preparation starts before the scanner: multilingual videos on the patient's own phone showing the room, the breath-hold and the sound. Six languages, no headset.

pillars.name: Scan faster
pillars.what: AI reconstruction rebuilds the same images from less data, so the scan ends sooner. Up to half as long on spine and brain protocols; about a third shorter on our own scans. Images come out sharper and less noisy, and our radiologists prefer reading them.

audit_numbers.limitation: Studies negative on both AI and report were not re-read, so sensitivity is likely overestimated. That limit is printed on the summary.

scan_time_arithmetic: The five to ten minutes either side of a scan - preparation and recovery - do not shorten. What shortens is the scan itself. On a twenty-minute scan, halving the scan takes ten minutes off a thirty-minute slot, not fifteen.
costs: No licence line is being asked for. The 3D service already runs at S$82-299 per reconstruction. The case for the rest is capacity, not cost saving: a shorter scan is a slot returned, and a film read sooner is a bed released.
dose: 4D imaging is a pilot with no outcome data yet. Dose targets are 0.1 mSv at the wrist and 1.0 mSv at the elbow.

patients.pRIMe: 16 of 16 patients reported a better experience at one month.
patients.principle: A scan that is not aborted is a scan we do not have to repeat.

governance.who_decides: The radiologist, always. The AI flag orders the work; it does not write the report. A flag that contradicts the on-call clinician goes to the radiologist first, not to the patient.
governance.not_replacing: No. Our own audit shows the tool missed seven fractures a radiologist caught. It buys time and orders the list; it does not read the film.
governance.extra_scans: None. Every programme reuses or shortens a scan already commissioned.
governance.staff_time: Training is minutes, not days: the flag appears where the film already opens.

cases.mr_lim: A man in his seventies who fell at home at three in the morning and cannot bear weight on his right knee. CT showed a coronal split fracture through the lateral tibial plateau; dual-energy CT revealed the bruise inside the bone. The surgeon plans the fixation in three dimensions from the same scan.
cases.ms_tan: 74, first MRI, a lump in her neck, claustrophobic, speaks Hokkien. pRIMe lets her rehearse the scanner on her phone before she arrives; MRI acceleration shortens the scan itself.
